_comment: Verification harness for the review of PR #400 (a DOCUMENTATION PR). Every finding is a doc-vs-implementation divergence, so every test is a bug-canary: it PASSES on the code under review and FLIPS TO RED once the divergence is resolved. See README.md for the observed-vs-expected table and per-finding fix sketches.

live._note: Exits 0 while the documented absolute maxSkew still bricks the RBG.

findings.claim: Doc says scaling.maxSkew accepts an absolute number (e.g. 2); parsePercentage requires a '%' suffix, so an absolute value aborts the whole RBG Reconcile.
findings.alsoLayer: l2 (scripts/l2-crd-accepts-absolute-maxskew.sh) proves the CRD does not reject it either

findings.claim: Doc says coordinated scaling only affects first deployment; there is no first-deployment gate, so steady-state scale-up (HPA/ScalingAdapter) is throttled identically.
Guide says rollingUpdate.maxSkew: 1 means 'at most 1 instance of skew'; the base is the literal 100, so an integer N is identical to "N%".
Doc body's batch-2 walkthrough claims {prefill:2, decode:3}; the implementation yields {prefill:1, decode:2}.
Guide claims each batch creates '1 decode and 2 prefill'; no batch ever does (max prefill delta per batch is 1).
Doc says progression defaults to OrderScheduled; there is no CRD default, so an omitted value is "" and canProceedToNextBatch skips the batch gate entirely.

Applying the documented absolute form scaling.maxSkew: 2 is accepted by the apiserver with no warning, then the RBG creates ZERO pods and stays READY=False; the only clue is a FailedCalculateScaling event. Changing only that value to "100%" yields READY=True and all 4 pods Running.
findings.note: Sharpens F1 from 'reconcile aborts' to a measured total failure with no apply-time signal.

liveNote: Round 2 (2026-08-05): the live layer is now available. The blocker was a controller-image lag -- the cluster ran v0.8.0-cea2a47 (commit cea2a472, 23 commits behind main, older than #394) which wrote restartPolicy as a bare string while the already-correct CRDs required an object, so no Pod was ever created. Fixed with: helm upgrade rbgs deploy/helm/rbgs -n rbg-system --set controller.features.portAllocator.enabled=true (chart 0.8.0-alpha.3, image rolebasedgroup/rbgs-controller:v0.8.0-47cfe17). Cluster: v1.36.1-aliyun.1, 3 nodes. No data migration was needed because the cluster held zero RoleInstanceSets -- do not assume that next time. F1 is now confirmed live (see results/l3-absolute-maxskew.txt). F2 (coordinated scaling is not limited to first deployment) is the next most valuable finding to take live -- its consequence, HPA-driven scale-out being throttled without an obvious cause, is most convincing when observed on a cluster. Not attempted this round. F3-F11 remain unit-level.
